correctness.rationale: Directly reconstructed all five proof steps. For a^(p+1)=a, e=a^p is idempotent, x=a-e lies in eAe and has x^p=0; converse follows from Frobenius binomial identity. The explicit unit e d_S+(1-e)(1-d_S) conjugates diagonal idempotents and yields exactly q^cut fibers; corners are induced incidence algebras. Product of p radical elements requires a chain of p+1 vertices. At the sharp first forbidden chain, the sole top-right entry of x^p is the product of p immediate superdiagonals, yielding exactly (q-1)^p q^(p choose 2) exceptions. For taller induced posets, a selected chain gives a nonzero degree-p polynomial, so Schwartz-Zippel yields the O(q^(m-1)) bound; the remaining leading terms are precisely antichain deletions of height at most p. Height positivity is proved by rank-layer antichains. Direct exhaustive tests of nine prime-field and two GF4 cases passed, but general proof is symbolic.

value.rationale: The characteristic dividing k is the mathematically motivated missing boundary of a direct incidence-algebra enumeration literature. The theorem classifies every solution over all finite fields for all height-at-most-p posets, identifies the precise first obstruction in a natural chain family, and supplies a global height-sensitive leading coefficient represented by antichain transversals. These are exact natural invariants, not parameter relabeling or tiny finite improvements.
